sections.h2: Rowlett, the lake and the county line
sections.html:
Rowlett is a lakeside city of about 22 square miles in the Dallas area, mostly in Dallas County with a western edge in Rockwall County. Dalrock Road is the county dividing line, so the county that handles your taxes depends on which side of that road your house sits on.

Lake Ray Hubbard, a reservoir and recreational lake, surrounds the city on two sides. Water on two sides shapes buyer interest, and a shoreline house can raise different insurance and survey questions than one inland.

sections.h2: Selling a Rowlett house in a hurry
sections.html:
Three paths cover most situations: an agent listing, a direct sale to an investor, or a sale to someone who plans repairs. Weigh how soon you need money against how much work the house needs.

  • A listing suits a house in showing condition when you can wait on lender approval and appraisal.
  • A direct investor sale fits a house with deferred work, a rental history or a tenant who cannot leave quickly.
  • A renovator sale is for homes with code issues or dated systems.

Collect two written offers and learn who pays closing costs. A house that has been rented needs the registration check in the next section.

Rowlett requires annual registration of single-family houses and duplexes used as rentals, and an inspection applies when tenants change. A buyer may ask whether a former rental is registered and current.

  • Annual registration is $50.00 per property.
  • An inspection is required at each tenant change, and the new tenant cannot move in until it passes. The inspection fee is $75.00.
  • If a tenant moves in before approval, the owner is charged $200.00.
  • The water utility account must be current, and a floor plan is required with the application.

Short-term rentals face tighter rules. The city adopted a short-term rental ordinance in April 2025, with a $2,000 annual application fee and permits that expire January 31. A 1,000-foot separation requirement applies to short-term rentals, applications are first-come, and owners must file hotel occupancy tax quarterly, including zero filings. Platforms like Airbnb and VRBO do not collect or remit that tax for Rowlett.

An owner running a short-term rental should tell buyers about the permit status, because the permit is tied to the owner and the property.

Anyone planning to keep the house as a short-term rental should read the conditions before making an offer. Only online applications are accepted, and the city partners with an outside platform to administer permits and hotel tax.

  • A designated local contact who is reachable 24 hours a day.
  • Notice to all residential properties within 200 feet.
  • A site plan, floor plan, parking plan and emergency evacuation plan.
  • A guest safety sheet displayed inside, and signage on the exterior near the front door.
  • A city inspection approved before anyone occupies the property, with short-term rentals inspected quarterly through the MyGov portal.
  • Current hotel occupancy tax filings.

A separate 1,000-foot rule bars renting to a registered sex offender within 1,000 feet of places where children commonly gather, and it applies to both short and long-term rentals. Complaints about a short-term rental can be made by phone or online through the platform the city names.

sections.h2: Property taxes split between two counties
sections.html:
Because Rowlett lies in Dallas and Rockwall Counties, a house is appraised by Dallas Central Appraisal District or Rockwall Central Appraisal District, depending on location. Check your tax statement to see which district and which county tax office applies.

Dallas CAD lets a homeowner who moves away temporarily keep the exemption if no other principal residence is set up and a return is planned within two years, with longer allowed for military service abroad or a care facility stay.

Dallas CAD also explains a tax deferral for owners who qualify by age or disability. Payment of taxes is postponed while you own and live in the home, but the tax is not cancelled, and five percent interest accrues each year. When the property is sold or transferred to an estate or heirs, the taxes and interest become due. Raise this with the title company, since it will be paid from proceeds.

sections.h2: Texas tax dates that matter when you sell in Rowlett
sections.html:
Texas uses one calendar for every city: appraisals are as of January 1, bills go out around October 1, and tax unpaid after January 31 is delinquent.

Texas property tax dates for Rowlett owners
DateWhat happens
January 1Values set and the tax lien attaches
April 30Last day for most exemption applications
May 15Last day to file most protests, or later if the notice came late
October 1Tax bills are mailed
February 1Unpaid tax is delinquent, penalty and interest start

sections.h2: Applying for a Dallas CAD homestead exemption
sections.html:
The applicant has to own and occupy the home on January 1 of the application year, and Dallas CAD asks for a copy of a Texas driver's license or ID whose address matches the homestead address. A buyer should know that the ID address must be changed at a state driver license office after closing.

  • A single or married owner may be able to apply online.
  • Each individual owner who lives there, apart from married couples, completes a separate application, and the exemption is split by percent of ownership.
  • Any rented or non-homestead part of the property, such as a room over a garage, must be listed by square footage.
  • For a house inherited without a recorded deed in the heir's name, the heir supplies an affidavit, the owner's death certificate, a recent utility bill and any court record citation.

Filing a homestead application is free. False statements or claiming homestead on more than one property is a crime under the Penal Code.

A permit is not needed for a sale, but past work should have been permitted. Rowlett runs an online permitting system for permit applications and contractor registrations. Ask the city's building safety staff if you are unsure about work done on your house.

sections.h2: Foreclosure or an inherited Rowlett house
sections.html:
In either case, call a title company early. A lender's foreclosure sale is set for a first Tuesday after a notice period. An estate needs the right deed or court order recorded with the clerk of the county that holds the land, either Dallas or Rockwall.

For a house you are selling after a death or while behind on payments, the buyer will want paper that shows who may sign the deed. Ask the title company what it will require, and have the water account, any rental registration and a tax statement ready before you list.

faqs.q: Which county records my Rowlett deed?
faqs.a: Whichever county holds the land. Most of Rowlett is in Dallas County and a western part is in Rockwall County, with Dalrock Road as the dividing line, so check your tax statement.

faqs.q: Do I have to register a rental house before selling it?
faqs.a: Rowlett requires annual registration of rental single-family houses and duplexes, at $50.00 per property. If the house is currently rented, ask the city whether registration is current before you list.

faqs.q: Is a short-term rental permit transferable to a buyer?
faqs.a: Ask the city before you promise anything. The permit is tied to the owner and the property, with a January 31 expiration and a 1,000-foot separation rule.

faqs.q: Can I postpone property tax and still sell?
faqs.a: Yes, if you qualify for the deferral that Dallas CAD describes for older or disabled owners. The postponed tax plus five percent annual interest comes due when the home is sold.

faqs.q: How long does a Rowlett cash sale take?
faqs.a: Timing depends on how fast title is cleared and the deed recorded. Liens, an unpaid rental registration or an inherited title can lengthen it.
